vignette: Layla, a 21-year-old woman of Middle Eastern descent, works as a forester in a national park near her hometown. Though she loves the outdoors and finds solace in nature, her life has been profoundly affected by an incident that occurred last year. It was early spring when Layla witnessed the trauma first-hand. She had gone on a routine inspection trek through dense forest with her colleague, Amir. Suddenly, they heard loud commotion-shouts and screams from nearby campers. They rushed to investigate and found a group of hikers in chaos: one man lay unconscious at the bottom of a steep ravine, another was shouting for help while holding his bleeding arm. Amir ran down to assist the injured man while Layla called emergency services. The scene was chaotic; people were panicking, and it felt like an eternity before help arrived. When the paramedics finally appeared, they whisked away the injured hikers, leaving a surreal silence in their wake. Ever since that day, Layla has been haunted by intrusive thoughts and images of the accident. Every time she hears loud noises or sees people in distress, memories flood back, causing her heart to race and sweat to break out on her forehead. She often finds herself checking her surroundings for potential threats during her patrols, which distracts her from focusing on her work. The trauma has also affected Layla's sleep. At night, she experiences vivid nightmares where the accident replays over and over again. These nightmares leave her feeling exhausted and anxious in the morning. Sometimes, she wakes up gasping for air or screaming, which can be jarring for her roommates. She often avoids sleeping alone to feel safer. Layla's relationships have also suffered due to her heightened state of alertness. When friends invite her out to social events, Layla feels overwhelmed by crowds and loud noises, making it difficult for her to enjoy herself or engage in conversations without feeling like she is missing cues from her environment. She has started to isolate herself more frequently, preferring the solitude of nature where she can feel a sense of control. Despite these challenges, Layla continues her work as a forester because it provides a grounding presence and offers an escape from her intrusive thoughts. Her daily routines in the forest-planting saplings, monitoring wildlife-help distract her momentarily from the lingering trauma. Layla also finds herself frequently avoiding specific areas of the park where she witnessed the accident. If she passes by that part of the trail or sees it on a map, she experiences intense distress and may have to leave the area immediately. This avoidance has limited her ability to explore certain parts of the park, which frustrates her as she believes these areas are vital for her work. In moments of quiet reflection, Layla wonders if she will ever fully recover from this experience. She feels a deep sense of guilt for not being able to do more during the accident and struggles with feelings of inadequacy because her once-clear mind is now clouded by intrusive thoughts and flashbacks. Despite these challenges, Layla remains committed to her work, hoping that immersing herself in nature will provide some relief from her symptoms. She continues to seek small moments of peace amidst the turmoil she faces each day.
